newsitem.title: RUSSIA: St Petersburg says close to Eurobond credit rating.
newsitem.headline: St Petersburg says close to Eurobond credit rating.

text.p: St Petersburg, which plans to issue a eurobond, is close to an agreement with a leading rating agency on a credit rating, authorities in Russia's second city said on Thursday.
The agreement, with either Standard & Poor's or Moody's Investors Services, would be concluded soon, the city council's press service said.
City governor Vladimir Yakovlev signed an order earlier this month on preparatory work for the eurobond issue.

Authorities in the Baltic city of five million have previously said they would issue bonds of up to $300 million through U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers. They would have a maturity of between two and five years.

St Petersburg already has a prolific municipal note programme on the Russian domestic market, and in April mandated Salomon to sell up to $200 million of short-term municipal paper to foreign investors.

The Russian Federation is preparing its debut eurobond in November, for which it has received speculative ratings, and the city of Moscow and Sverdlovsk region have also outlined plans to issue eurobonds.
